perspectives.author: metav3rse
perspectives.title: Linus Torvalds started Linux in 1991 as a personal project while studying computer science in Finland. What began as something he built for himself grew into one of the most important pieces of software in the world, powering cloud servers, supercomputers, Android devices, and much of the internet. The bigger idea was open source. Thousands of developers could contribute, improve the code, and build something together without one company controlling it. Credits: The Linux Foundation
